intended_object: The trivial natural transformation H ⟶ G between functors C ⥤ Grp: each component is the trivial homomorphism sending every element to 1. This is the zero morphism of the functor category. The docstring says so, and the quotient construction uses it as the second arrow of a cokernel cofork.
explanation:
At each object, the component is the group homomorphism x ↦ 1. Naturality holds because every map in the square sends everything to 1. So this is exactly the trivial (zero) natural transformation between group-valued functors, as the docstring says.

Mathlib has no ready-made counterpart. `GrpCat` gets a `HasZeroObject` instance in `Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Zero.lean`, but there is no `HasZeroMorphisms` instance for `GrpCat` or for functor categories into it. Zero morphisms could only be obtained through a non-instance construction such as `zeroMorphismsOfZeroObject`.

The same construction would also work for functors into monoids (`MonCat`). However, the library uses it for quotients of group functors, where it serves as the second arrow of the cokernel cofork. Group-valued functors are the natural setting for that, so the definition is not too narrow in any meaningful sense.
